object.odia: ଷାଠିଏ ବାଟି ନାହାକିଆଣୀ ପରର ବାଡ଼ି ପନ୍ଦାଡ଼ରେ ମାଗି ଖାଉଛି
object.title: Land and a meal from elsewhere
object.literal_meaning: The woman with sixty bāṭi of land asks for food at another’s yard or veranda.
object.explanation: The dictionary defines a woman with extensive landholdings. The quotation sets that description beside asking and eating elsewhere. Our reading notices a gap between an imposing description of possessions and the immediate means of obtaining a meal. It leaves the reason open rather than declaring the woman dishonest or undeserving.
object.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ବହୁ ଜମିର ଅଧିକାରିଣୀ ସ୍ତ୍ରୀଙ୍କୁ ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। ଉଦ୍ଧୃତି ସେହି ପରିଚୟ ପାଖରେ ପରଘରେ ମାଗି ଖାଇବାକୁ ରଖେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ସମ୍ପତ୍ତିର ବଡ଼ ପରିଚୟ ଓ ସେହି ବେଳର ଖାଇବା ଯୋଗାଡ଼ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଫରକ ଦିଶେ। ଏହାର କାରଣ ଖୋଲା ରହେ; ସ୍ତ୍ରୀଜଣକ ଠକ ବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ଆମେ ରାୟ ଦେଉନାହୁଁ।
object.english_summary: Our reading distinguishes possessions from the meal immediately available.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ସମ୍ପତ୍ତି ଓ ସେହି ବେଳର ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଯୋଗାଡ଼କୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: କଥାଟି ପଢ଼ି ଜଣେ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଜମି ଅଛି ବୋଲି ସେହି ବେଳେ ଖାଇବା ଅଛି କି?” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କହିଲେ, “ଏଠି କାରଣଟା ଲେଖାନାହିଁ।” / Two readers distinguish owning land from having a meal available and leave the missing explanation unresolved. Their discussion is invented.
object.cultural_context: The female landowner is the source’s subject. Bāṭi is retained without conversion; the line establishes neither a historical person nor a cause of her request.

object.odia: ନାଟର ଗୁରୁ ଗୋବର୍ଦ୍ଧନ ଦାସ
object.title: The director behind the action
object.category: dictionary-labelled Dhaga headword idiom; source-informed editorial reading
object.literal_meaning: Gobardhan Das, the master of the play.
object.explanation: The dictionary defines a concealed controller: others visibly act, while this person directs them. The theatrical wording identifies the person behind the action, not a documented theatre practitioner. Our application asks who actually makes a decision when somebody else announces it; hidden direction need not be guessed from appearances alone.
object.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଏମିତି ଜଣେ ସୂତ୍ରଧରଙ୍କୁ ବୁଝାଏ, ଯିଏ ନିଜେ ଚିହ୍ନା ନପଡ଼ି ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କ କାମକୁ ଚଳାନ୍ତି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ହେଉଛି—ଖବର ଦେଉଥିବା ଲୋକ ଓ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନେଉଥିବା ଲୋକ କିଏ? କେବଳ ଚେହେରା ଦେଖି ଲୁଚା ସୂତ୍ରଧର ଥିବାର ଅନୁମାନ କରିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: A named theatrical idiom points to concealed direction behind visible action.
object.odia_summary: ଆଗରେ କାମ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପଛରେ ଥିବା ସୂତ୍ରଧରକୁ ଏହି ପଦଟି ବୁଝାଏ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: ମୀନା ସଭାରେ ନୂଆ ସମୟ ଘୋଷଣା କଲେ। ରବି ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଏହି ସମୟ କିଏ ଠିକ୍ କଲା?” ମୀନା ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତିର ଚିଠି ଦେଖାଇଲେ। / Meena announced a new meeting time. Ravi asked who had chosen it, and she showed him the decision letter. This invented scene explores responsibility; it does not establish a secret plot.
object.cultural_context: The source labels the whole headword Dhaga and supplies its figurative meaning. Gobardhan Das remains part of the expression; this page does not identify a historical individual, author or origin. Bengali and Hindi equivalents are listed, not evidence of transmission direction.

object.odia: ବୁଢ଼ା ଚୋରକୁ ଚୋରି ଶିଖଉଛି !
object.title: Teaching the practised thief
object.literal_meaning: Teaching an old hand at theft how to steal!
object.explanation: The dictionary places this exclamation under a thief practised in the activity, separately from an elderly thief. Its joke makes the lesson unnecessary because the learner already knows the craft. Our everyday application questions instruction offered without first finding out what someone knows; it neither praises theft nor says experienced people cannot learn.
object.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନର ଏହି ଅର୍ଥରେ ଚୋରଟି ଚୋରିରେ ପାରଙ୍ଗମ; କେବଳ ବୟସରେ ବୁଢ଼ା ନୁହେଁ। ଯିଏ କାମଟି ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣେ, ତାକୁ ସେହି କାମ ଶିଖାଇବାରେ କଥାର ମଜା। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ଶିଖାଇବା ଆଗରୁ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କେତେ ଜାଣନ୍ତି, ତାହା ବୁଝିବା ଦରକାର। ଏହା ଚୋରିର ପ୍ରଶଂସା ବା ଅଭିଜ୍ଞ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଆଉ ଶିଖିବାର ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ରାୟ ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: An unnecessary lesson becomes the joke; our application asks about prior experience.
object.odia_summary: ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିଥିବା କାମ ଶିଖାଇବାକୁ ନେଇ ମଜା; ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ପୂର୍ବ ଅଭିଜ୍ଞତାକୁ ଜାଣିବା ଜରୁରୀ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: ନୂଆ ସହକର୍ମୀ ଫାଇଲ ସଜାଇବା ଶିଖାଇବାକୁ ଯାଉଥିଲେ। ରୀତା କହିଲେ, “ଏହି ପଦ୍ଧତିଟା ମୁଁ ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲି; ତୁମ ପାଖରେ କିଛି ନୂଆ ଉପାୟ ଅଛି କି?” / A colleague begins explaining a filing method to its creator, who remains open to improvements. This scene is invented.
object.cultural_context: The saying accompanies sense1, proficiency through practice. Sense2 separately describes an elderly thief. Neither establishes a real offender or an age-group trait.

object.odia: ଯାହା ଘରେ ରହେ ଯୁବା ଝିଅ, ବିନା ନିଆଁରେ ପୋଡ଼େ ତା ଦିହ
object.title: Burning without fire
object.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: Whoever has a grown daughter at home burns in body without fire.
object.explanation: The line makes a grown daughter’s presence the occasion for burning without flame. It does not state marriage, dowry, a cause of distress or an actual injury. Our critical response refuses to turn that charged comparison into a verdict that daughters are burdens. Asking whose worry is being voiced leaves the young woman’s own perspective open.
object.meaning_odia: ବଢ଼ିଲା ଝିଅ ଘରେ ଥିବା ସହିତ ନିଆଁ ବିନା ଦେହ ପୋଡ଼ିବାର ତୀବ୍ର ଛବି ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଏଠି ବିବାହ, ଯୌତୁକ, ଦୁଃଖର କାରଣ ବା ପ୍ରକୃତ ଆଘାତ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠ ଏହାକୁ ଝିଅମାନେ ବୋଝ ବୋଲି ରାୟ କରେନାହିଁ। କାହାର ଚିନ୍ତା ଏଠି କୁହାଯାଉଛି ବୋଲି ପଚାରିଲେ ଝିଅଟିର ନିଜ ଦୃଷ୍ଟିଭଙ୍ଗୀ ପାଇଁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଜାଗା ରହେ। ଦେହଟି କାହାର, ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେନାହିଁ; ଏହି ପାଠ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ, ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: Our critical response questions the burden implied by the fireless-burning image.
object.odia_summary: ନିଆଁ ବିନା ପୋଡ଼ିବାର ଛବିରେ ଥିବା ବୋଝର ଇଙ୍ଗିତକୁ ଆମ ପାଠ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଏଠି କାହାର ଚିନ୍ତା?” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କହିଲେ, “ଝିଅଟି ନିଜେ କଣ କହିବ, ସେଥି ବି ଶୁଣିବା ଦରକାର।” / Readers ask whose anxiety the line expresses and leave room for the daughter’s voice. Their discussion is invented, not a collected traditional explanation.
object.cultural_context: The dictionary defines a daughter who has reached puberty. The pronoun’s bodily subject is not further explained; the literal reading remains provisional. No present-day family or community trait is established.

object.odia: ଦେଖାଦେଖି ଚାଷ, ଲଗାଲଗି ବାସ
object.title: Near enough to attend to
object.literal_meaning: Cultivation where it can be regularly seen; dwellings close together.
object.explanation: The accompanying adjective means something that can often be seen or attended to. The line pairs that accessibility in cultivation with proximity in living. Our reading asks what distance permits us to notice and care for; it does not prescribe settlement density or promise better harvests.
object.meaning_odia: ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ବିଶେଷଣର ଅର୍ଥ—ଯାହାକୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଦେଖି ବା ତାହାର ତତ୍ତ୍ୱ ନେଇହେବ। ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଚାଷରେ ସେହି ସୁବିଧା ସହିତ ଲଗାଲଗି ରହିବାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଆମ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ, ଦୂରତା କେଉଁ କାମର ତତ୍ତ୍ୱ ନେବାରେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ବା ବାଧା ଦିଏ। ଏହା ଘରବସତିର ନିୟମ ବା ଭଲ ଫସଲର ନିଶ୍ଚୟତା ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: Our reading connects proximity with the possibility of regular attention.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ପାଖରେ ଥିବାକୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର ତତ୍ତ୍ୱ ନେବାର ସୁବିଧା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠାଗାରର ମରାମତି ଖାତାଟି ଦୂର ଆଲମାରିରେ ରହୁଥିଲା। ସ୍ୱେଚ୍ଛାସେବୀମାନେ ତାହାକୁ କାମର ଟେବୁଲ ପାଖରେ ରଖିଲେ, ଯେପରି ରୋଜ ଦେଖିପାରିବେ। / Volunteers move a repair log near their worktable so they can check it daily. This practical analogy is invented.
object.cultural_context: This is the adjective-sense example, separate from the earlier river/kinship saying and later named literary line. No agricultural trial or universal village pattern is established.

object.title: You turned away from me
object.literal_meaning: Newness lasts how many days? Seeing the new, you forgot the old and turned your back on me.
object.explanation: The speaker protests being forgotten when something new appears. The source places the saying under neglect, but identifies neither the relationship nor the new attraction. object.title: An unexpected claimant
object.literal_meaning: Even when there is no rival, an unexpected claimant appears.
object.explanation: The headword defines an unexpected rival, enemy or claimant to a share. The saying contrasts apparent absence with sudden arrival. Our application notices how a settled expectation can be interrupted; it does not prove that the newcomer’s claim is false or that every undertaking must meet opposition.
object.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ହଠାତ୍ ଆସୁଥିବା ପ୍ରତିଦ୍ୱନ୍ଦ୍ୱୀ, ଶତ୍ରୁ ବା ଭାଗ ଦାବି କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। କେହି ନଥିବା କଥା ପାଖରେ ହଠାତ୍ କେହି ବାହାରିବା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ଧରିନିଆ କଥା କିପରି ବଦଳିପାରେ, ତାହା ଦିଶେ। ନୂଆ ଲୋକର ଦାବି ମିଛ ବା ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ କାମରେ ବିରୋଧୀ ଆସିବେ ବୋଲି ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।

object.title: A ring does not change the blow
object.literal_meaning: A slap from a gold-ringed hand brings the benefit of bathing in the Ganga.
object.explanation: The saying gives a blow from an adorned hand the value of a sacred bath. Our critical reading questions that elevation: an ornament does not make harm deserved or beneficial. This is our response to the line, not a supplied traditional counter-moral or a claim of ritual efficacy.
object.meaning_odia: ସୁନାମୁଦି ପିନ୍ଧା ହାତର ଚାପୁଡ଼ାକୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଗଙ୍ଗାସ୍ନାନର ଫଳ ସହିତ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠ ସେହି ମୂଲ୍ୟଦାନକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ—ଅଳଙ୍କାର ଥିବାରୁ ଆଘାତ ଯୋଗ୍ୟ ବା ଉପକାରୀ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଏହା ଆମ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା; ଉତ୍ସରେ ଦିଆଯାଇଥିବା ପାରମ୍ପରିକ ବିପରୀତ ଉପଦେଶ ବା ଧାର୍ମିକ ଫଳର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: Our critical response separates an adorned hand from any justification for its blow.

object.title: A household’s changing circumstances
object.literal_meaning: At times, a home with two wives; at times, blow and blow at the hearth until you die.
object.explanation: The repeated “at times” turns a household image into an exhausting cooking complaint. The source gives no cause for the change. object.title: The nearby voice
object.literal_meaning: The one who sleeps nearby speaks into the ear—can their words be distrusted?
object.explanation: The question gives a nearby voice an apparent advantage. The dictionary places it under backbiting, making access to the listener part of the image. Our reading separates that closeness from reliability: being heard privately does not establish that a report is true. No spouse, gender or actual accusation is identified.
object.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ସ୍ୱରକୁ ଏକ ସୁବିଧା ଦେଉଥିବା ପରି ଲାଗେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଚୁଗୁଲି କହିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ନିକଟତାକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱସନୀୟତାଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ—ଏକାନ୍ତରେ ଶୁଣିଲେ ବୋଲି କଥାଟି ସତ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ବକ୍ତା ପତି ବା ପତ୍ନୀ, କେଉଁ ଲିଙ୍ଗର ବା କେଉଁ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରୁଛନ୍ତି, ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ।

object.title: The fish advertises its worth
object.literal_meaning: The bhakuda fish said: I am king among fish; make broth from my head and see how enjoyable it is.
object.explanation: The talking fish supports its royal claim with an offer of its own head for cooking. Our reading follows that odd self-advertisement: praise of its worth comes through what someone else might enjoy. This is a playful reading of the boast, not a supplied moral about sacrifice or a tested cooking recommendation.

object.title: Someone else wears the blame
object.literal_meaning: The villagers ate the jackfruit; they smeared its sticky substance on Bhandari’s head.
object.explanation: The eaters and the person marked by the sticky residue are different. The headword explicitly explains laying blame or stigma on someone. Our reading follows that transfer: the visible mark is made to point away from those who acted. It is a way to question an accusation, not evidence about any community’s conduct.
object.meaning_odia: ପଣସ ଖାଇଥିବା ଲୋକ ଓ ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ ଅଠା ବୋଳାଯାଇଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଅଲଗା। ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥରେ କାହା ଉପରେ ଦୋଷ ବା କଳଙ୍କ ଦେବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଦାଗଟି ପ୍ରକୃତ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକାରୀଙ୍କ ବଦଳରେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷୀ ଦେଖାଉଛି। ଏହା ଅଭିଯୋଗକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବାର ପାଠ, କୌଣସି ସମୁଦାୟର ଆଚରଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।

object.title: A hard division between working and asking
object.literal_meaning: Whoever works does not eat by asking; whoever eats by asking does not earn food through work.
object.explanation: The paired clauses draw an absolute line between labour and asking for food. The headword supplies earning a livelihood through work. Our critical response questions the absolute division: the saying does not establish why anyone needs help or whether their work meets their needs. That response is editorial, not a counter-moral supplied by the dictionary.
object.meaning_odia: ଧାଡ଼ି ଦୁଇଟି ପରିଶ୍ରମ କରି ଖାଇବା ଓ ମାଗି ଖାଇବାକୁ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଲଗା କରିଛି। ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥରେ ପରିଶ୍ରମ କରି ପେଟ ପୋଷିବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପାଠ ଏହି କଠୋର ବିଭାଜନକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ। କିଏ କାହିଁକି ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ମାଗୁଛି ବା ତାହାର କାମରୁ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ମେଣ୍ଟୁଛି କି, ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ତାହା ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ। ଏହି ପ୍ରତିପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଆମର, ଅଭିଧାନର ଉପଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ।

object.title: Praise that turns to revulsion
object.literal_meaning: Extraordinary beauty; seeing you makes me feel like vomiting.
object.explanation: The apparent praise turns sharply into rejection. The dictionary places the saying under figurative revulsion, separate from its physical sense. Our reading hears an insulting reversal, not a reliable description of someone’s appearance. A speaker’s disgust does not establish another person’s worth, and the line supplies no relationship or occasion.

object.odia: ଭାତ ଥିଲେ ଭାତୁଆ ଅପୂର୍ବ?
object.title: Rice and the people who serve
object.literal_meaning: If there is rice, are people serving for food hard to find?
object.explanation: The question connects available food with the availability of a servant. The dictionary supplies both serving-for-food and servant senses. Our critical reading asks what is lost when a person’s labour is reduced to a meal. The wording does not establish that workers are plentiful everywhere, that food is adequate payment, or that anyone owes service for being fed.
object.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ଭାତ ଥିବା ସହ ସେବା କରିବା ଲୋକ ମିଳିବାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଅନ୍ନ ପାଇଁ ସେବା କରୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଓ ଚାକର ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ: ଜଣଙ୍କ ଶ୍ରମକୁ କେବଳ ଭୋଜନରେ ମାପିଲେ କଣ ଅଦେଖା ରହେ? ସବୁଠି କର୍ମୀ ସହଜରେ ମିଳନ୍ତି, ଭୋଜନ ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ପାରିଶ୍ରମିକ, କିମ୍ବା ଖାଇଥିବାରୁ ସେବା ଦେବାକୁ ହେବ—ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଏସବୁର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: Our response distinguishes feeding someone from valuing their work.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା ଖାଇବାକୁ ଦେବା ଓ ଶ୍ରମର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଦେବାକୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।

The line does not establish deception, betrayal or an unfair intention; it makes the different positions audible without explaining why they arose.

object.title: Rice, or age?
object.literal_meaning: Is rice making that person impudent, or is age doing it?
object.explanation: The question offers two explanations for conduct the speaker regards as impudent. That meaning comes from the dictionary’s third sense. Our critical reading pauses before accepting either explanation: a question can carry a judgment without proving its cause. Neither eating rice nor belonging to an age group establishes how someone behaves.

object.title: Heavy stones, and a plea from cotton
object.literal_meaning: The grinding slab and stone are flying in the sky; silk-cotton fluff says, “Keep me safe.”
object.explanation: The dictionary places the saying under the figurative sense of heavy things. Even the grinding stones are aloft, while light fluff asks to be kept safe. object.title: Cut off food, cut off life
object.literal_meaning: Stopping someone’s food and cutting off their head are called the same thing.
object.explanation: The dictionary places the saying under stopping someone’s food. Its stark comparison gives deprivation the force of a threat to life. Our reading treats that equivalence as rhetorical emphasis on food’s importance, not a clinical equation or an instruction to injure anyone. The line does not identify who withholds food or describe an actual incident.
object.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବନ୍ଦ କରିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ତୀବ୍ର ତୁଳନାଟି ଖାଦ୍ୟରୁ ବଞ୍ଚିତ କରିବାକୁ ଜୀବନ ପ୍ରତି ବିପଦ ପରି ଦେଖାଏ। ଆମ ପାଠ ଏହାକୁ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଉପରେ ଜୋର ବୋଲି ବୁଝେ, ଚିକିତ୍ସାଗତ ସମାନତା ବା କାହାକୁ ଆଘାତ ଦେବା ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ। କିଏ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବନ୍ଦ କଲା ବା ସତରେ କଣ ଘଟିଲା, କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
object.english_summary: Our reading takes the food-deprivation warning seriously without literalizing its violence.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଖାଦ୍ୟରୁ ବଞ୍ଚନାର ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦେଖେ, ହିଂସାକୁ ଆକ୍ଷରିକ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ କରେନାହିଁ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: ସମୂହ ଭୋଜନର ତାଲିକାରେ କାହାର ନାମ ଛାଡ଼ିଗଲା କି ନାହିଁ ଦଳଟି ପୁଣି ଦେଖିଲା। / Organizers check that nobody has been omitted from a shared meal. This scene is invented.
object.cultural_context: Sense1 is distinct from eating smaller portions in later senses. No dietary, medical or financial recommendation, verified deprivation event or traditional charity rule is supplied.

object.odia: ଶହେ ଭାକା, ଏକଲେଖା
object.title: A hundred utterances, one writing
object.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: a hundred utterances, one written record.
object.explanation: The source places this compact fragment under matter committed to writing. Our reading understands the contrasting term as spoken utterances, but the head does not separately gloss it. The numbers set many beside one; no verb supplies a precise equation or legal rule. We read an invitation to consider what writing preserves, not proof that every written statement is true.
object.meaning_odia: ଲିଖିତ ବିଷୟ ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଉତ୍ସ ଏହି ଛୋଟ ଖଣ୍ଡଟି ରଖେ। ଭାକାକୁ ମୁହଁର କଥା ଭାବେ ନେଇ ଆମେ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ ଦେଉଛୁ; ଏହି ଶବ୍ଦର ଅଲଗା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏଠି ନାହିଁ। ସଂଖ୍ୟା ଅନେକ ପାଖରେ ଗୋଟିଏକୁ ରଖେ, କିନ୍ତୁ କ୍ରିୟା ନଥିବାରୁ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ସମୀକରଣ ବା ଆଇନର ନିୟମ ମିଳେନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠ ଲେଖା କଣ ରଖିପାରେ ଭାବେ, ସବୁ ଲେଖା ସତ ବୋଲି ମାନେନାହିଁ।
object.english_summary: Our provisional reading compares speech and writing without inventing a full rule.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ କଥା ଓ ଲେଖାକୁ ତୁଳନା କରେ, ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ନିୟମ ଗଢ଼େନାହିଁ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଆଲୋଚନା ପରେ ଦଳଟି ଠିକ୍ ହୋଇଥିବା କାମଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଲେଖିଲା ଓ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ପୁଣି ପଢ଼ି ଶୁଣାଇଲା। / A group writes and checks its agreed tasks together. This application is invented.
object.cultural_context: Exact ଭାକା and fused ଏକଲେଖା remain unchanged. Other sayings and Krishna Singh literary examples in this long head are separate witnesses, not this fragment’s authorship.

object.title: Coming and going alone
object.literal_meaning: You came alone and will go alone; the family will not go with you.
object.explanation: The repeated solitude stands against the family named in the final phrase. The dictionary gives family members, including children, as the relevant sense. Our reading hears a reflection on mortality and the limits of accompaniment. That interpretation does not make family affection worthless, require withdrawal from loved ones, or prove a doctrine about what follows death.
object.meaning_odia: ପୁଣିପୁଣି ଆସୁଥିବା ଏକାପଣ ପାଖରେ ଶେଷ ଖଣ୍ଡ ପରିବାରକୁ ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କ ସହ ପରିବାରସ୍ଥ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ଏଠି ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ଓ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ରହିପାରିବାର ସୀମା ନେଇ ଭାବନା ଶୁଣେ। ଏହା ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା; ପରିବାରର ସ୍ନେହ ମୂଲ୍ୟହୀନ ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ। ପ୍ରିୟଜନଙ୍କୁ ଛାଡ଼ି ରହିବା ବା ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ପରେ କଣ ହୁଏ ସେବିଷୟରେ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ମତ ମଧ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: Our reading holds life’s limits beside the value of present companionship.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଜୀବନର ସୀମା ସହ ବର୍ତ୍ତମାନର ସାଙ୍ଗତ୍ୟର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ରଖେ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପଢ଼ି ଜଣେ ପ୍ରିୟଜନଙ୍କ ସହ ସମୟ କାଟିବାକୁ ଠିକ୍ କଲେ। / A reader responds by making time for loved ones. This response is invented, not a traditional use claim.
object.cultural_context: Arrival and departure are the quoted images; mortality is our interpretive frame. The later Fakirmohan example illustrates another sense and does not identify the saying’s author.

object.title: The father rides; the son, a little
object.literal_meaning: Whose father rides a horse, that son rides a little.
object.explanation: The rhyme moves from a father’s riding to a smaller amount in the son’s clause. The dictionary quotes it under “slightly; a little.” Our reading notices the partial echo between generations, without turning it into a law of inheritance. The line does not explain how either person learned, measure their skill, or establish that every child repeats a parent’s occupation.
object.meaning_odia: ବାପଙ୍କ ଘୋଡ଼ା ଚଢ଼ିବାରୁ ପୁଅଙ୍କ ଖଣ୍ଡରେ ଅଳ୍ପ ପରିମାଣକୁ ଛନ୍ଦ ଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ସାମାନ୍ୟରେ ବା ଈଷତ ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ପିଢ଼ି ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଆଂଶିକ ପ୍ରତିଧ୍ୱନି ଦେଖେ, ବଂଶଗତ ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ। କିଏ କିପରି ଶିଖିଲେ, କାହାର ଦକ୍ଷତା କେତେ, ବା ସବୁ ପିଲା ବାପମାଆଙ୍କ ପେଶା ନିଅନ୍ତି କି ନାହିଁ—ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ତାହା ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
object.english_summary: Our reading hears a small repetition, not an inherited destiny.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଅଳ୍ପ ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତି ଶୁଣେ, ବଂଶଗତ ଭାଗ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: ବାପଙ୍କ ସହ କାମ ଦେଖିଥିବା ପୁଅଟି ନିଜେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଛୋଟ କାମ ଶିଖିଲା। ତାଙ୍କ ଅନ୍ୟ ପସନ୍ଦକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ପରିବାର ସ୍ଥାନ ଦେଲା। / A child learns one small task while retaining other interests. This scene is invented.
object.cultural_context: The quotation’s father and son remain intact, without an added biological or caste claim. The earlier Radhanath Darbar verse illustrates a different sense and is not this saying’s authorship.

object.odia: ସେ ହଗ ନାହିଁ କି ବାଟ ଛାଡୁ ନାହିଁ
object.title: Neither doing it nor making way
object.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: that person neither shits nor makes way.
object.explanation: The blunt bodily image pairs not doing something with not letting another pass. The dictionary supplies making room for another as the relevant sense of leaving the way. Our reading applies the contrast to obstruction: someone neither proceeds nor clears space. This does not identify a real person’s health, intention or circumstances, and it is not advice about bodily functions.
object.meaning_odia: ରୁକ୍ଷ ଶାରୀରିକ ଚିତ୍ରଟି ନିଜେ ନ କରିବା ସହ ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ବାଟ ନ ଛାଡ଼ିବାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଯିବାକୁ ଜାଗା ଦେବା ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଉତ୍ସର ହଗ ଶବ୍ଦରୂପ ଅବିକଳ ରଖି ଆମେ ଏହାର ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ ଦେଉଛୁ। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ କେହି ନିଜେ ଆଗେଇନାହାନ୍ତି କି ଜାଗା ମଧ୍ୟ ଛାଡ଼ୁନାହାନ୍ତି। ଏଥିରୁ ପ୍ରକୃତ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ସ୍ୱାସ୍ଥ୍ୟ, ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ବା ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ। ଏହା ଶରୀର ସମ୍ବନ୍ଧୀୟ ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: Our reading describes obstruction while keeping the coarse register visible.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ବାଧାକୁ ଦେଖାଏ, ରୁକ୍ଷ ଭାଷାକୁ ଲୁଚାଏନାହିଁ।

object.title: Naming the rain amid the flood
object.literal_meaning: The house is flooded, the water knee-deep; the one-eyed person says it is raining in torrents.
object.explanation: The house and knee-deep water show a consequence; the speaker names the rain. The dictionary explicitly glosses torrential rain, not a light shower. Our reading asks whether naming an event is enough when its effects need attention. We reject using the quoted disability label to explain anyone’s judgment: the line supplies no evidence that impaired sight causes such a response.
object.meaning_odia: ଘର ବୁଡ଼ି ପାଣି ଆଣ୍ଠୁଏ; ବକ୍ତା ବର୍ଷାର କଥା କହୁଛନ୍ତି। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଦୁଲୁକିବା ଅର୍ଥ ପ୍ରବଳ ବର୍ଷା, ଅଳ୍ପ ବର୍ଷା ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ: ପ୍ରଭାବକୁ ଦେଖି କାମ କରିବା ଦରକାର ବେଳେ ଘଟଣାର ନାମ କହିବା ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ କି? ଉତ୍ସର ଦୃଷ୍ଟିସମ୍ବନ୍ଧୀୟ ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟକୁ ଆମେ ବିଚାରଶକ୍ତିର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଭାବେ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରୁନାହୁଁ। ଏପରି ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟାର କାରଣ ଦୃଷ୍ଟିବାଧା ବୋଲି ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।

object.literal_meaning: Being taken by a tiger does not hurt; the dragging hurts.

object.title: One keeps; another will squander
object.literal_meaning: The books say: one will squander; one is keeping.
object.explanation: The saying invokes books while putting keeping beside future squandering. object.title: Let the visits continue
object.literal_meaning: Let the coming and going continue; let there be no hope of a handful of rice.
object.explanation: The line wishes for continued visits while setting aside an expectation of rice. Its dictionary placement concerns frequenting a place. Our reading values contact beyond what a visit might provide. That application is editorial: the source names no particular friendship, household or exchange, and it does not require a hungry guest to deny their needs.
object.meaning_odia: ଯିବାଆସିବା ଚାଲିଥାଉ, କିନ୍ତୁ ମୁଠିଏ ଭାତର ଆଶା ନ ଥାଉ—ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଏହି ଇଚ୍ଛା କହେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ବାରମ୍ବାର କୌଣସି ସ୍ଥାନକୁ ଯିବା ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ପ୍ରାପ୍ତିର ଆଶାଠାରୁ ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦେଖେ। ଏହା ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ; ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ବନ୍ଧୁତା, ପରିବାର ବା ଦେଣନେଣ କହେନାହିଁ। ଭୋକିଲା ଅତିଥି ନିଜ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ଲୁଚାଇବାକୁ ବାଧ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: Our reading separates continued contact from an expected material return.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଯିବାଆସିବା ଓ ପ୍ରାପ୍ତିର ଆଶା ଅଲଗା ରହେ।

object.title: Six ears and a disclosed secret
object.literal_meaning: Six ears, disclosure of the secret.
object.explanation: The dictionary explains six ears as three people: a matter known to two reaches a third. The short saying compresses that disclosure into a phrase. Our reading notices how adding a listener changes the circle of knowledge. It does not prove that every third person spreads a secret or forbid seeking appropriate help about something troubling.
object.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଛଅଟି କାନ ଅର୍ଥ ତିନି ଜଣ: ଦୁଇ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଗୁପ୍ତ କଥା ତୃତୀୟ ଜଣ ଜାଣନ୍ତି। ଛୋଟ ଢଗଟି ସେହି ପ୍ରକାଶକୁ ଧରେ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଆଉ ଜଣେ ଶୁଣିଲେ ଜାଣିଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପରିସର ବଦଳେ। ସବୁ ତୃତୀୟ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି କଥା ପ୍ରଚାର କରନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। ଚିନ୍ତାଜନକ ବିଷୟରେ ଉପଯୁକ୍ତ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ମାଗିବାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଏହା ବାରଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
object.english_summary: Our reading tracks a wider circle, not inevitable betrayal.
object.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଜାଣିବାର ପରିସର ବଢ଼େ, ବିଶ୍ୱାସଘାତ ଅନିବାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।

object.title: A question about complexion
object.literal_meaning: Dark woman, does applying lime make you fair?
object.explanation: The question places a woman’s dark complexion beside an applied white substance. object.odia: ଥାଇକରି ଯେ ଖାଇମନ କରେ ତା ମୁହଁଟା ପୋଡ଼ୁ
object.title: A curse directed at craving
object.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: may the mouth of one who craves while having be burnt.
object.explanation: The headword defines wanting a particular food. The line curses someone described as having yet craving; it does not specify what is possessed or establish that their needs are met. Our critical reading separates a speaker’s accusation from knowledge of another’s circumstances. Neither the curse nor the accusation becomes advice about how a person should eat.
object.meaning_odia: ଖାଇମନ କରିବାର ଅର୍ଥ କୌଣସି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଇଚ୍ଛା କରିବା। ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଚାହୁଁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଅଭିଶାପ ଦିଏ। କଣ ଅଛି ବା ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ପୂରଣ ହୋଇଛି କି, ଉତ୍ସ କହେନାହିଁ; ଏହି ପାଠ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ କଥକଙ୍କ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଓ ଅନ୍ୟର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଜାଣିବା ଅଲଗା। ଅଭିଶାପଟି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବା ଆଚରଣର ପରାମର୍ଶ ନୁହେଁ।
object.english_summary: The accusation leaves the person’s possessions and actual needs unspecified.
object.odia_summary: କଣ ଅଛି ଓ କଣ ଦରକାର, ଅଭିଯୋଗଟି ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେନାହିଁ।
object.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ମାଗିବାରୁ ଜଣେ ଅତିଥିଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷ ଦିଆଗଲା। ଘରଲୋକ ପ୍ରଥମେ ତାଙ୍କ କଥା ଶୁଣିବାକୁ କହିଲେ। / An imagined host asks others to hear a guest’s reason before judging a request. This alternative is invented.
object.cultural_context: The later pregnancy sense does not identify this subject. The following Nilamani Chintatarangini passage is a separate literary illustration, not this saying’s author.
